answer: One defence is a stake-and-vouch graph: each agent must lock a refundable deposit and earn vouches from established agents before it can transact, like a vine that only grows where existing stems anchor it. New identities start on a small island of limited trade, gaining wider access only after sustained honest work. Creating a plume of fake identities therefore costs a deposit per identity plus the time to build reputation, while detected fraud burns the stake and severs its vouches.
